methods.notes: Substring match, mirroring the community scanner. The buds advertise only while out of the case (removing them powers them on; placing them in the case powers them off) and only while not connected to a phone. Expect TWO results per pair — one per bud — with different addresses. On macOS the address is an ephemeral CoreBluetooth UUID that can change between sessions.

identification.notes: LOW confidence matcher. The factory advertised name was not recorded by any source; the community client finds buds by looking for "bose", "sleepbud" or "drowsy" anywhere in the name, case-insensitive, and the owner can rename the buds in the app (a flag in the Settings characteristic records that this happened), so a renamed pair will not match. Whether the Bose member service 0xfe21 is in the advertisement is unknown; if a scan shows it is, that is the better axis.

device.name: Bose Sleepbuds II
device.notes:
Tiny in-ear buds that play stored noise-masking sounds all night; they stream nothing from the phone. The phone's only job was to run the Bose Sleep app, which over BLE picked the sound, set the volume and timer, set alarms, toggled phone-free mode and uploaded new sound files. Bose discontinued the product in 2023 and withdrew the Sleep app from both app stores on 2025-07-21, ending its development; an installed copy keeps working until a phone OS update breaks it, and Bose's only suggestion is to enable phone-free mode first so the buds play one preselected sound on their own.
`manufacturer_status: abandoned` rather than `shutdown` because Bose is very much in business — it is this product and its app that were dropped, with no replacement path (the Ozlo Sleepbuds Bose points owners at are a different company's product and do not control these buds).
The buds are TWO BLE peripherals. The left and right bud each advertise, each accept one connection, and each must be written separately; the left bud does not relay to the right. The vendor app held two connections and sent every command to both. This spec therefore describes one bud; a consumer treats each bud as its own device and the user pairs the two up by name.
What this spec covers: picking which stored sound plays, volume, start and stop, the playback timer, battery, the phone-free flag, and the alarm and synchronised-start opcodes as far as they are known. What it deliberately does NOT cover: uploading sound files (the "TUMBLE" chunked transfer with CRC-32 confirmation on the control point) and firmware update (the same control point plus a binary-packet characteristic, and a legacy OTA service). Both are documented well enough in SleepBuds2Revival to be revisited; they are out of scope here because they write to the buds' storage and nothing about them has been checked beyond one author's bench.
Firmware 11.x units ("Kingsley") are the Sleepbuds II. The same app also drove the 2018 first-generation noise-masking sleepbuds ("Drowsy", firmware 6.x/7.x), which use an 8-byte playback frame and a different set of sound file IDs. Where the two differ this spec says so, but the first generation is not otherwise covered.

openness.notes: Bose published nothing about the BLE interface. One community client (February 2026, no licence) recovered it from the Sleep app and checked the playback path on a Sleepbuds II pair. No second independent implementation is known; treat every fact here as resting on that single source until someone replays it.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: No button and no pairing mode. A bud advertises whenever it is out of the case and not connected; the owner's guide's "power on" is simply removing it from the case.

exclusivity.recovery: Force-stop the Bose Sleep app if installed; on an iPhone also forget the Sleepbuds in Settings > Bluetooth and toggle Bluetooth off and on (Bose's own disconnect instruction); put both buds in the case until the lights blink white and take them out again; then connect.

pairing.notes: The evidence points two ways and neither source settles it. FOR a bond: Bose tells iPhone owners to forget the Sleepbuds in the iOS Bluetooth settings, and iOS only lists BLE accessories it has paired with; the buds reconnect to "the most recently connected device" on power-up; the control point's response-code table includes an "already bonded" code. AGAINST a mandatory bond: the community client connected and wrote playback frames from a macOS host without describing any pairing prompt (though macOS pairs silently when a characteristic demands encryption, so this proves little); the owner's guide never shows a passkey or a Bluetooth-settings step and the buds have no button or display, so any pairing that does happen can only be Just Works. Until someone watches the SMP exchange, implement for both: connect, and accept a Just Works bond if the stack asks.

unpair.notes: There is no factory reset at all, so a stored peer can only be dropped from the phone side if it is dropped at all. Bose's disconnect instructions are phone-side (forget in iOS Bluetooth settings; disconnect in the Android app). Whether the bud then accepts a new phone without further ceremony is unverified — the community client connected from a Mac that had never run the app, which is weak evidence that it does.

credentials.notes: No application-layer secret exists: the writable characteristics take plain frames with no token, PIN or key.
stored_on_device: Peer record for the most recently connected phone (a bond, if the link is bonded — see pairing)
Device name set by the owner
Phone-free flag and the sound, volume and timer it replays
Stored sound files (file IDs listed by the Sounds characteristic)

factory_reset.description: Two things exist that are NOT a factory reset and get mistaken for one. (1) The charging case has a pinhole on its back next to the USB-C port; pushing a straightened paper clip in until it clicks powers the case off and on, which Bose offers for charging problems only. (2) Placing the buds in the case and waiting for the charging lights to blink slowly white, then taking them out again, power-cycles the buds; Bose's troubleshooting step for a bud that misbehaves. To make a bud forget a phone there is no bud-side procedure: forget it in the phone's Bluetooth settings (iOS) or disconnect it in the app (Android), then power-cycle the buds via the case.
factory_reset.effect: None. Bose's support article for the Sleepbuds II states that there is no factory reset for this product; the buds have no button and no documented way to clear their stored state or pairings on the device itself.

methods.description: Take the buds out of the case, connect to one of them, subscribe to the notifying characteristics, and read the state characteristics the vendor app read after connecting. The read of the Audio Data characteristic matters: the playback frame carries the current file ID, which `set_volume` needs. Repeat for the other bud. Nothing is written during this flow except an optional connection-interval request.
methods.name: Connect to each bud and read it

steps.action: Close or force-stop the Bose Sleep app if it is still installed, and disconnect any other client; each bud accepts one connection.
Remove both buds from the charging case and wait a few seconds; they power on and advertise.
Scan and connect to one bud by address. Accept a Just Works pairing prompt if the host raises one.

Enable notifications on the Control Point e81359e0-9f35-483a-a46f-7c6d686daa06, the Settings characteristic 5e500c28-33db-4d0a-afc8-c9b6df4269bf and the Audio Data characteristic 1cbd5f8f-6c18-4309-9354-703e7d42a74e.
Read firmware revision 00002a26-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb and serial number 00002a25-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb.
steps.expect: Firmware as text, e.g. 11.9.0. A serial ending in -Kde marks Sleepbuds II (Kingsley) hardware.

steps.action: Read the Settings characteristic, the Sounds characteristic 12a3d434-c7de-4760-88c0-4f743ea55e98 and the Audio Data characteristic.
steps.expect: 4 bytes of flags and battery; a list of stored file IDs ending 0xffa0; a 12-byte playback frame.

steps.action: Optionally write the connection-parameter request (opcode d0 00) to the Control Point to ask for a faster interval; a response of 00 or 08 is fine.
Repeat for the other bud. Commands are per bud; send a play frame to both to hear it in both ears.

setup.notes: Nothing to provision: a bud out of its case advertises, and a central that connects can read everything and write playback frames. The one open question is link-layer — see `pairing`: the phone the vendor app ran on appears in iOS's Bluetooth list, which suggests a bond is formed, but the community client never reports a pairing prompt and the owner's guide never mentions one. Close the Bose Sleep app first if it is still installed; a bud serves one central at a time.

rejoin.notes: BLE only; there is no network to rejoin. Any central may connect once the current one disconnects and, if a bond is in play, once the previous phone has forgotten the bud. The buds reconnect on their own to the most recently connected device when they power on within about 2 m of it.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. Every byte below comes from one community client (SleepBuds2Revival) whose author decompiled the Bose Sleep app and then exercised the result on one pair of Sleepbuds II running firmware 11.9.0. Frames marked `reported` are ones that author drove on the bench or lifted from the app; `hypothesis` marks layouts the client constructs but never reports having had accepted.

entities.name: Sound
entities.notes: Picking an option starts that sound at the command's default volume (50) on THIS bud. The options are the Sleepbuds II catalogue; a bud holds only the subset its Sounds characteristic lists, so a consumer that can read that list should hide the rest. The five alarm tones are left out of the picker.

entities.name: Volume
entities.notes: Read-modify-write: set_volume needs the file ID currently in bytes 2-3 of the characteristic, and BLE command parameters have no read-back source in this schema, so a generic consumer cannot send it without device-specific code. Shown for the state; the control works only in a consumer that fills file_id from its last read.

entities.name: Time Remaining
entities.notes: 0 while an untimed sound plays or nothing plays.

entities.name: Phone-Free Mode
entities.notes: Turning this on makes the bud play its stored phone-free sound at its stored volume every time it leaves the case, with no phone involved — the one thing Bose suggests owners do before the app dies. On the bench it started an unknown sound at volume 100; warn before enabling.

artifacts.description: Python/bleak client plus PROTOCOL_REFERENCE.md derived from Bose Sleep app 3.0.11 and tested on firmware 11.9.0 Kingsley hardware from a macOS host. Source of every UUID, frame layout and opcode here and of the per-bud write-type finding. No licence file; facts were derived and restated, no code copied.

evidence.documentation_review: Read 2026-10-11. SleepBuds2Revival's reference and source agree with each other on every UUID and layout used here; its own notes flag two internal inconsistencies (retry counts, and whether the control point might also exist under 0xfe21 on older firmware) which are reflected as caveats rather than facts. Bose's support pages and the owner's guide supplied the product status, the absence of a factory reset, the power-on/off and reconnect behaviour and the phone-side disconnect steps; neither says a word about BLE security. The bosefirmware/eb index ties the "drowsy" codename to the 2018 first-generation product.
evidence.open_questions: Whether the link is bonded (and Just Works) or open; the factory advertised name and whether 0xfe21 is advertised; the alarm write payload and the alarm read reply; the Sounds header bytes; the phone-free sound and volume storage (where the vendor app set them); whether play_in_future fails with both buds connected because of the buds or because of macOS; whether Battery Level notifies.

dfu_mode.notes: No separate bootloader advertisement is known: the bud stays in its application GATT while receiving an image, and what it advertises during or after activation has not been observed.

enter.notes: The running application takes the image itself: data is written to the Binary Packet characteristic 86d60053-6f4a-409c-9a81-93f16c4e15a0 inside the normal control service, then the advanced command activate_firmware (Control Point opcode 0x08, sub-module 0x01) switches to it. The transfer format over Binary Packet is not documented by any source; the community client only exercised the activation query and received the no-image error.

image.notes: The Bose Sleep app fetched images from Bose; the app is withdrawn and no public image URL is known, so in practice no image is obtainable. Whether the bud checks a signature is not established: the activation error table has a bad-CRC code, which is an integrity check, not authentication.

dfu.notes: Declared so a consumer knows the bud takes firmware over BLE and keeps generic controls away from the Binary Packet and legacy OTA characteristics. From the community reference derived from Sleep app 3.0.11; the legacy OTA service 4b25c5ad is listed because the app still knew it, with no evidence of which firmware uses it.

recovery.notes: Nothing published. The control service c76e1666 is NOT listed under services above because it also carries the Control Point used for ordinary playback control; only the Binary Packet characteristic inside it belongs to the update path.

AudioFrame.description: The 12-byte Audio Data frame, read or written whole; the same layout as that characteristic's format block, with the two frames the community client logged.
parse_rules: 01 32 4f 7b 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 decodes as: playing, volume 50, file ID 0x7b4f = 31567 (Warm Static), no timer, no fade.
00 00 a0 ff 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 is the stop frame: stopped, volume 0, file ID 0xffa0 (none).
A write shorter than 12 bytes is rejected by firmware 11.x with ATT error 0x42.

ControlPointResponse.description: Notification from the Control Point after a write: status, then the opcode and sub-module of the frame it answers.

fields.description: Byte 0: 0x00 success, 0x02 not supported, 0x03 invalid parameter, 0x04 parameter update failed, 0x05 rejected, 0x06 timeout, 0x07 already bonded, 0x08 already in requested state, 0x09 timing error, 0x0c busy, 0xff general failure.
fields.name: status

parse_rules: 03 01 bb is INVALID_PARAM to a play_in_future (01 bb).
Replies to firmware-activation and file-transfer frames carry further status bytes; not covered.

PlayInFuture.description: The 18-byte synchronised-start frame built from a Sync read, as the control point's play_in_future template renders it.
parse_rules: From Sync read 00 0d 01 00 65 01 00 00 (01 min 00 s 357 ms 0 us): add 750 ms -> 1107 ms -> carry: 01 min 01 s 107 ms.
Frame for Warm Static at volume 50, untimed: 01 bb | 01 01 6b 00 00 00 | 00 | 4f 7b | 32 | 00 00 | 00 00 | 00 00.
This example is computed from the documented rule, not a captured frame; the author's accepted frames were not logged byte for byte.

SoundsList.description: Reply to a read of the Sounds characteristic 12a3d434-c7de-4760-88c0-4f743ea55e98.

fields.description: From byte 4: little-endian uint16 file IDs, one per stored sound.
fields.name: file_ids

fields.description: 0xffa0 (a0 ff on the wire) ends the list.
fields.name: terminator

parse_rules: Skip 4 header bytes, then read uint16 LE values until 0xffa0 or the end of the value.

IDs from the Kingsley catalogue (31567, 13198, ...) mark Sleepbuds II; IDs from the Drowsy catalogue (8278, 14373, ...) mark a first-generation bud. The vendor app's small internal track numbers are odd for Kingsley and even for Drowsy; the file IDs on the wire follow no such rule.

SyncClock.description: Reply to a read of the Sync characteristic 1cbe5f90-6c19-430a-9355-703f7d43a74f.
parse_rules: 00 0d 01 00 65 01 00 00 decodes as: type 0, 13 h 01 min 00 s, 357 ms (0x0165 LE), 0 us.

bud_time.in_play_in_future: bytes 2-7 of the frame are minutes, seconds, ms, us (hours dropped), then one zero pad byte at offset 8
bud_time.layout: 7 bytes: hours, minutes, seconds, milliseconds u16 LE, microseconds u16 LE
bud_time.offset_rule: add ~750 ms to the clock just read, carrying ms -> s -> min; all-zero timing is refused with status 0x09, mis-indexed timing with 0x03

sub_modules.0: system queries (firmware versions 0x3d/0x3a/0x3b, update status 0x3c) and connection parameters (0xd0)
sub_modules.3: TUMBLE file transfer (0x01-0x0b) — out of scope

out_of_scope.firmware_update: The activation frame is declared as the advanced command activate_firmware and the path as features[type: firmware_update]; what stays out of scope is the image transfer itself, which no source documents. Image data goes to the Binary Packet characteristic 86d60053-6f4a-409c-9a81-93f16c4e15a0. The legacy OTA service 4b25c5ad-978d-467c-b598-155247b9e774 carries command 7ee6acc4-884c-4d97-ab3a-26c99459c030, state b7488798-dd0d-40d2-8372-96524b495b47, image block 47bbaf32-049e-44d2-ac33-a131fc73f8bd, status 2c54d3b1-aedc-47ec-82c7-27bb68b6a0e6 and image info 43246004-5173-4f20-96e2-d594472d828b. None of the transfer is covered; do not send the activation frame to a bud you want to keep.
out_of_scope.sound_upload: TUMBLE transfer on the Control Point, sub-module 0x03: create a sound and file entry, stream 32 KiB clusters as 16-byte packets, confirm each cluster's CRC-32 (sent as a u64 LE), end with the whole-file CRC-32. Audio is raw 8192 Hz 24-bit little-endian mono PCM, one file per bud. Documented in SleepBuds2Revival; not covered here.

sound_catalogue_first_generation.note: First-generation noise-masking sleepbuds (Drowsy, firmware 6.x/7.x) store these file IDs and take an 8-byte playback frame (bytes 0-7 of the Sleepbuds II frame); not otherwise covered by this spec. The app's internal track numbers, never sent on the wire, are even for this generation and odd for Sleepbuds II.

sync_opcodes.note: Single-byte writes to the Sync characteristic recovered from the app; none exercised by the community client, so not declared as commands.

two_peripherals.fcc_ids: A94432893L (left) and A94432893R (right), model S08SEE6M1A, per the device.report listing of grantee 432893.
two_peripherals.summary: Left and right buds are independent BLE peripherals with their own addresses, serials and state; nothing is relayed between them.
two_peripherals.vendor_app_behaviour: Held two connections and sent every write to both buds, one after the other.
two_peripherals.write_type_quirk: On the one pair tested the left bud needed write-without-response on Audio Data and the right bud write-with-response; the other type was rejected (ATT 0x42) or silently ignored respectively. Try with-response, fall back to without-response.

remaining_unknowns: Firmware: the image transfer format over the Binary Packet characteristic, whether images are signed, and what a bud advertises during an update are unknown; only the activation opcode and its no-image error reply are recorded.

Link-layer security: no source has watched the pairing exchange. iOS lists the buds (suggesting a bond) but the community client never mentions pairing from macOS. pairing.required is therefore 'unknown'.
The factory advertised local name; the identification matcher is a low-confidence guess from the community scanner's substrings, and a renamed pair will not match it.

Volume cannot be set without re-sending the current file ID, and this schema has no BLE read-back source, so the Volume number entity is not drivable by a generic consumer — the same gap AM43's battery reply hit.
alarm_set's payload layout is a hypothesis from the community client's code; no acceptance was reported. The alarm_read reply layout is unknown.
Where the vendor app stored the phone-free sound and volume. Enabling the flag on a bud whose stored state was unknown played an unidentified sound (file ID 30325) at volume 100.
Sound file upload (TUMBLE, sub-module 0x03) and firmware update / activation (sub-module 0x01, Binary Packet, legacy OTA service) are deliberately out of scope; SleepBuds2Revival documents both.
Whether play_in_future's INVALID_PARAM with two simultaneous connections is a bud limitation or a macOS CoreBluetooth artefact.
First-generation (Drowsy) buds: the 8-byte frame and the separate file-ID catalogue are noted, but no first-generation unit has been exercised by any source read.

characteristics.name: Firmware Revision String
characteristics.notes: UTF-8 text such as 11.9.0. Firmware 11.x requires the 12-byte playback frame; the first-generation 6.x/7.x firmware used an 8-byte one.

characteristics.name: Serial Number String
characteristics.notes: Per-unit serial. A suffix of -Kde marks Sleepbuds II ("Kingsley") hardware, which is the only way besides the stored file IDs to tell the two generations apart before writing anything.

services.name: Device Information
services.notes: Standard SIG service. Three characteristics are known to answer. The serial number identifies one unit; log the suffix, not the value.

services.name: Battery Service
services.notes: Standard SIG battery service, read by the community client. Whether the level also notifies was not recorded. The Settings characteristic carries a second copy of the percentage at byte 1.

play_sound.description: Start a stored sound on this bud, untimed, no fade. Warm Static (file ID 31567) at volume 50 renders as 01 32 4f 7b 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00, the frame the community client logged as accepted. Send to both buds for both ears.

file_id.description: File ID of a sound stored on this bud, little-endian; take it from the Sounds characteristic. Not the app's small track number — the firmware ignores those.

volume.description: Volume byte. The wire accepts 0-255 but the vendor app never exceeds 100 and 100 is already very loud in-ear; bounded here for hearing safety.

play_sound_timed.description: Start a stored sound with a sleep timer: masking_timeout and time_remaining both set to the duration, after which the bud stops on its own.

duration.description: Play duration; written to both the timeout and the remaining field.

file_id.description: File ID of a stored sound, little-endian.

set_volume.description: Change the volume of what is playing. There is no volume-only write: the community client reads the 12-byte frame, replaces byte 1 and writes it back. This template is that frame for an untimed sound, so the caller must supply the file ID read from the characteristic (bytes 2-3); a consumer with no read-back path should use play_sound with the user's chosen sound instead.

file_id.description: The file ID currently in bytes 2-3 of the characteristic — read it first.

stop.description: Stop playback: state 0, volume 0 and the no-sound sentinel 0xffa0 as the file ID, which is the frame the vendor app and the community client both send.

format.name: volume
format.notes: Raw 0-255; the vendor app's range is 0-100.

format.name: file_id
format.notes: File ID of the current or last sound. The table is the Sleepbuds II (Kingsley) catalogue known to the community client; a bud only holds the subset the Sounds characteristic lists, and an owner who uploaded other sounds will show IDs outside it. 0xffa0 (65440) is the vendor's "no sound" sentinel. The first-generation catalogue is in protocol_details.

format.name: masking_timeout
format.notes: Total play duration; 0 = play until stopped or returned to the case.

format.name: time_remaining
format.notes: Counts down from masking_timeout; the client sets it equal to masking_timeout when starting a timed sound.

characteristics.name: Audio Data (playback state)
characteristics.notes:
Twelve bytes, little-endian, read and written whole. Firmware 11.x rejects the older 8-byte frame (the write fails with ATT error 0x42). The sound is addressed by its FILE ID — the large number the Sounds characteristic lists — not by the app's small internal track number; a frame carrying a track number is accepted and silently ignored.
WRITE TYPE DIFFERS PER BUD, on the one pair tested: the left bud took write-without-response and rejected write-with-response with ATT error 0x42; the right bud silently ignored write-without-response and acted only on write-with-response. Try write-with-response first and fall back to write-without-response if it errors; that sequence worked on both. The vendor app presumably lets the Android stack pick.
Writing a frame with state 1 starts the sound immediately on this bud only. Volume is a raw byte 0-255 of which the app uses 0-100; one test at 100 was described as painful, so clamp. A read while stopped returns the last file ID with state 0.

characteristics.name: Sounds (stored file list)
characteristics.notes: Variable length: a 4-byte header (observed 01 00 02 00, meaning unknown) followed by little-endian uint16 file IDs and terminated by 0xffa0. These are the IDs play_sound accepts. Layout in payload_formats.SoundsList. Which generation a bud is can be read off this list: Sleepbuds II units hold IDs from the Kingsley catalogue (31567, 13198, ...), first-generation units IDs from the Drowsy one (8278, 14373, ...). The two sets do not overlap, but neither follows a parity or range rule.

characteristics.name: Sync (bud clock)
characteristics.notes: Reads 8 bytes: a type byte then the bud's 7-byte clock (payload_formats.SyncClock). The synchronised-start command on the Control Point copies five of those bytes plus an offset. The vendor app also writes single-byte sync opcodes here (protocol_details.sync_opcodes); none was exercised by the community client and they are not declared as commands.

services.name: Audio service
services.notes: Bose's playback service. Audio Data is the whole everyday control surface — one 12-byte frame says what plays, how loud and for how long, and reading it back returns the current state. Sounds lists what is stored; Sync exposes the bud's clock for the synchronised start on the control point.

phone_free_off.description: Clear the phone-free flag; the bud waits for a connected client again.

phone_free_on.description: Set the phone-free flag. The bud will then play its stored phone-free sound whenever it leaves the case, without any connection. See the characteristic notes for the volume surprise this produced on the bench.

characteristics.name: Settings (flags and battery)
characteristics.notes:
Four bytes. Byte 0 is a flag byte; byte 1 repeats the battery percentage; bytes 2-3 were always zero in the frames seen. The phone-free flag is the only bit known to be writable and the client writes the whole 4 bytes with the others zero.
Enabling phone-free mode makes the bud start its stored phone-free sound at the stored phone-free volume as soon as it is out of the case — on the bench that was an unknown sound at volume 100 in one ear. Disabling it stopped the sound. Treat the toggle with the same care as a volume write.

characteristics.name: Device Name
characteristics.notes: The advertised name, writable; the vendor app's rename feature. Listed under this service by the community reference even though the UUID is the GAP device-name characteristic. Renaming sets the `renamed` flag in Settings and breaks the name-based discovery matcher above.

services.name: Settings service (Bose member UUID)
services.notes: 0xfe21 is the Bluetooth SIG 16-bit UUID assigned to Bose. On the Sleepbuds it carries a 4-byte flags/battery characteristic and the writable device name. The community client's constants also place the control point here as a fallback for first-generation firmware; on Sleepbuds II it lives in the update service below.

activate_firmware.advanced_reason: Switches the bud onto whatever firmware image has been transferred to it. With a bad or partial image the bud may stop working, and no recovery path is documented; with nothing pending it only returns an error. Never send it to a bud you want to keep unless you have transferred a known-good image.
activate_firmware.description: Activate a firmware image already transferred to the bud (opcode 0x08, sub-module 0x01). Payload: a component mask, then the major, minor and patch of the image to activate, one byte each. Mask bits: 0x01 bud, 0x02 case, 0x04 radio, 0x40 set version only, 0x80 clear. With nothing pending the bud answers status 0x43 (activate error) followed by per-component status bytes; the community client saw 43 08 01 00 8d 01 40 02 40 from both buds, read as bud 0x8d (bad CRC / nothing pending), case 0x40 and radio 0x40 (idle). The image transfer that precedes this write (Binary Packet characteristic) is not documented by any source, and no success reply has been recorded.

component_mask.description: Bit mask of components: 0x01 bud, 0x02 case, 0x04 radio; 0x40 sets the version record only; 0x80 clears.

major.description: Major version of the image to activate.

minor.description: Minor version of the image to activate.

patch.description: Patch version of the image to activate.

alarm_cancel.description: Cancel the pending bud-based alarm (opcode 0x02, sub-module 0x02).

alarm_read.description: Read the pending bud-based alarm (opcode 0x00, sub-module 0x02). The reply layout has not been recorded.

alarm_set.description: Set a bud-based alarm (opcode 0x01, sub-module 0x02) that fires on the bud's own clock, so it works with the phone off. HYPOTHESIS: the opcode comes from the app, but the payload layout here is the one the community client constructs — file ID, volume, seconds from now (the app's limit was 18 hours = 64800), play duration, fade-in and fade-out, all little-endian — and no source reports the bud accepting it. Send alarm_read afterwards and check the status byte before trusting it.

file_id.description: File ID of the alarm tone, little-endian; the catalogue's alarm tones are 37901, 3632, 32302, 28072 and 9145.

seconds_from_now.description: Delay until the alarm fires; the app capped it at 18 hours.

cancel_play_in_future.description: Cancel a pending synchronised start (opcode 0x02, sub-module 0xbb).

play_in_future.description: Synchronised start — the vendor app's primary way to start a sound on both buds at the same instant. Sent to EACH bud's control point with timing derived from THAT bud's Sync clock. Opcode 0x01 on sub-module 0xbb; byte 8 is a zero pad. payload_formats.PlayInFuture has a worked example. A plain play_sound write to each bud is the fallback and simply starts them a few hundred milliseconds apart.

file_id.description: File ID of a stored sound, little-endian.

microseconds.description: Copied from the Sync clock, little-endian.

milliseconds.description: Target millisecond: the Sync clock's milliseconds plus about 750, modulo 1000, little-endian.

minutes.description: Target minute, from the Sync clock's minutes plus carry.

seconds.description: Target second, from the Sync clock plus carry.

query_case_firmware.description: Charging-case firmware version query (opcode 0x3b, sub-module 0x00). Reply layout not recorded.

query_radio_firmware.description: Radio firmware version query (opcode 0x3a, sub-module 0x00). Reply layout not recorded.

query_system_firmware.description: System firmware version query (opcode 0x3d, sub-module 0x00). Reply layout not recorded; the Firmware Revision String is the easier read.

query_update_status.description: Firmware-update status query (opcode 0x3c, sub-module 0x00). Reply layout not recorded.

request_connection_parameters.description: Ask the bud to change its connection interval (opcode 0xd0, sub-module 0x00): min and max interval in 1.25 ms units, slave latency, supervision timeout in 10 ms units, all little-endian. The community client sends 16/16/0/200 after connecting and accepts status 0x00 or 0x08 (already in that state). The vendor app's defaults were 120 (standard) and 16 (fast); Sleepbuds II file transfer used 15, first-generation units 30.

max_interval.description: Maximum connection interval in 1.25 ms units.

min_interval.description: Minimum connection interval in 1.25 ms units.

supervision_timeout.description: Supervision timeout in 10 ms units (200 = 2 s).

characteristics.name: Control Point
characteristics.notes: Write with response; subscribe before writing and wait for the status notification (payload_formats.ControlPointResponse). The vendor app retried a failed synchronised start up to three times. Timing bytes in play_in_future come from a fresh read of the Sync characteristic: copy minutes, seconds, milliseconds and microseconds (NOT hours — including hours shifts every field and earns status 0x03), then add about 750 ms with carry into seconds and minutes. All-zero timing earns status 0x09. The community client got status 0x00 from both buds when it connected to them one after the other, and 0x03 from both when it held both connections open at once on macOS; whether that is the host stack or the buds is unknown.

characteristics.name: Binary Packet (firmware data)
characteristics.notes: Carries firmware image data during an update: the update path declared in features[type: firmware_update]. The transfer format over it is not documented by any source, so nothing should be written here outside an update you understand. Listed so a reader knows what the characteristic is.

services.name: Update / control service
services.notes: Despite the name this service carries the vendor app's command channel for Sleepbuds II, not just firmware update. The Control Point takes [opcode][sub-module][payload] frames and answers with a notification [status][echoed opcode][echoed sub-module]; the sub-module byte selects a function group — 0x00 system queries, 0x01 firmware activation, 0x02 alarm, 0x03 file transfer, 0xbb audio. Only the audio, alarm, connection-parameter and system-query frames are declared below. The file-transfer (0x03) and firmware-activation (0x01) groups and the Binary Packet characteristic are the out-of-scope upload and DFU paths — see protocol_details.out_of_scope.

services.name: Legacy OTA service
services.notes: An older over-the-air update service the vendor app still knows (command, state, image-block, status and image-info characteristics; UUIDs in protocol_details.out_of_scope). Part of the update path declared in features[type: firmware_update]; not exercised by any source, so no characteristic is documented here and a generic client lists it read-only.
